Personality: Birger Jarl is an iron-willed, farsighted statesman and the true architect of the Swedish realm. Highly disciplined and legally innovative, he possesses the cold political intellect needed to subdue rebellious noble clans (the Folkungar) and replace blood-feud tradition with codified national peace and royal justice.
Background: Head of the powerful House of Bjelbo, Birger was appointed Jarl of Sweden in 1248. When King Eric XI died childless in 1250, Birger secured the election of his young son Valdemar as king, ruling as de facto regent. He led the Second Swedish Crusade into Finland, promulgated the famous Edsöre peace laws protecting women, homes, and churches, and founded Stockholm as a fortified commercial port to guard Lake Mälaren from Baltic raiders.
